source.title: Finite Versus Infinite Neural Networks: an Empirical Study
source.authors: Jaehoon Lee; S. Schoenholz; Jeffrey Pennington; Ben Adlam; Lechao Xiao; Roman Novak; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present
record.tranche_reason: The study compares finite and infinite networks and reports some training-accuracy outcomes, but it does not test the claim versions about nonlinear networks reaching near-zero training classification error under the listed recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper's principal results concern test accuracy and correspondence to kernel methods. Its explicit linearized CNN-GAP training-accuracy results are recorded under fits_no_version because linearized networks do not test the versions' claims about nonlinear networks.
record.test_reason: The record overlooks §C's achieved training-accuracy results: nonlinear CNNs trained with mini-batch SGD on CIFAR-10 met a stopping criterion above 99% accuracy on a random 5,000-example training subset at five checkpoints. These results bear on V1, although they do not establish full-training-set accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase accurately describes the linearized CNN-GAP finding and the paper's broader focus. It is incomplete as an account of claim-relevant training results: §C also reports that nonlinear CNN trials achieved the sampled training-fit criterion, with augmented CNN-VEC training among the exceptions.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses finite networks trained with mini-batch SGD and MSE, and also studies linearized networks and kernel inference. It does not test the claim's near-zero training classification-error outcome for nonlinear networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and parameterization affect reported test-accuracy outcomes; the paper does not map claim-specific training-error sensitivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Linearized CNN-GAP reaches only 86.22% training accuracy with STD parameterization and 79.90% with NTK parameterization after 14M steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linearized CNN-GAP models can converge extremely slowly because of poor conditioning.

record.problems: For the linearized CNN-GAP results, the paper reports best achieved training accuracy rather than a completed fit; the work does not evaluate the nonlinear training-error claims in the versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcomes were identified. Test-accuracy tables and figures do not measure the training-error behavior specified by the versions.

untested.parts: Full-training-set near-zero error; CIFAR-100 training outcomes; corrupted or random labels; systematic training-error comparisons across model sizes and early-stopping recipes. The magnitude of residual training error in augmented CNN-VEC runs is not reported.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, very deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup.
Comparisons of activation-matched initializations, signal propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.

Loss rise and recovery with curvature reduction above the initial stability threshold, larger-rate divergence in nonlinear networks, and edge-of-stability dynamics. Large-learning-rate test-accuracy comparisons do not establish these outcomes.
Batch normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance, and training without normalization using Fixup.

missing.what: Achieved stopping criterion for nonlinear CNN-VEC and CNN-GAP: above 99% accuracy on a random 5,000-example training subset at five logarithmically spaced checkpoints for c ≤ 1. Record architecture, parameterization, sampled measurement, and training recipe separately where identifiable.
missing.locator: §C, Finite width neural networks; §2 architecture specifications

missing.what: Data-augmented CNN-VEC training did not achieve the training-fit termination criterion; the authors report best achieved performance instead. No achieved training-accuracy value is supplied, so this cannot establish substantial residual error.

record.verdict_notes: The two extracted rows are correctly excluded from V1, but their exclusion does not justify classifying the entire study as non-testing. Most tabulated accuracy values are test accuracy and should not become training-error rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether sufficiently large nonlinear CNNs reach near-zero training classification error, or the stated effects of corrupted labels, model size, early stopping, or regularization.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum experiment or width comparison.
Does not compare depth or identity shortcuts; its tested architecture comparisons do not test the stated depth effect.
Uses ReLU with critical initialization but does not compare initializations or test trainable depth.
Includes large-learning-rate settings but does not report the loss-curvature and stability-threshold outcomes in this version.
Does not test batch normalization or Fixup.

rows.subject: linearized CNN-GAP, STD parameterization
rows.size_stated: 8 layers of 512 channels per layer (base CNN); linearized
rows.operation_detail: Trained the linearized network on CIFAR-10 with MSE; best achieved training accuracy is reported after 14M steps.
rows.note: This is a linearized network, so the result does not measure the nonlinear-network behavior specified by V1.
rows.check: The reported 86.22% training accuracy after 14M steps is correct. The model is linearized and therefore does not measure V1's nonlinear CNN training behavior.

rows.subject: linearized CNN-GAP, NTK parameterization
rows.size_stated: 8 layers of 512 channels per layer (base CNN); linearized
rows.operation_detail: Trained the linearized network on CIFAR-10 with MSE; best achieved training accuracy is reported after 14M steps.
rows.note: This is a linearized network, so the result does not measure the nonlinear-network behavior specified by V1.
rows.check: The reported 79.90% training accuracy after 14M steps is correct. The model is linearized and therefore does not measure V1's nonlinear CNN training behavior.

relationships.condition: Nonlinear CNN-VEC and CNN-GAP on clean CIFAR-10, without data augmentation, trained with mini-batch SGD and MSE at learning-rate factors c ≤ 1.
relationships.reason: Text-based verdict: §C reports achieving above 99% accuracy on a random 5,000-example training subset at five checkpoints; the record contains no rows for these nonlinear results.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy exceeded 99% on a random 5,000-example training subset at five checkpoints.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
